cards.title: Why and for whom
cards.description: Emperor: goal, users, scenarios, measurable outcome
cards.prompt:
Turn the confirmed hypothesis into a product brief. Analysis only — no code.

If idea validation did not pass — say to return to the “Idea check” deck. Spec without a confirmed idea is too early.

Output:
1. Goal (one sentence)
2. Who the user is (specific)
3. Key scenarios (3–5)
4. Measurable outcome in one month
5. What we will NOT do in v1

Forbidden: inventing users/scenarios outside the hypothesis; adding “for later” features.
Next: “What we do”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — brief is ready
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: What we do
cards.description: Two of Swords: IN / OUT, one happy path, acceptance
cards.prompt:
Lock the smallest working version. Analysis only — no code.

Output:
1. IN: what we do in v1
2. OUT: what we do NOT do
3. One happy path — from entry to result
4. Acceptance criteria
5. What we defer and why

Rules: cut anything the first path does not need. If IN has more than 5 features — cut. Do not add “might need later”. Do not invent requirements outside the brief.
Next: “How it looks”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — scope is ready
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: How it looks
cards.description: Ace of Cups: screens, controls, empty/loading/error states
cards.prompt:
Describe the UI in text. No code, no images.

Output: screen list; per screen — buttons and fields; empty / loading / error / success states; how screens connect.

Do not generate images, Figma, or markup. Do not add screens outside scope. More than 5 screens — consider merging. Must be buildable with simple means.
Next: “What we store”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — UI described
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: What we store
cards.description: Ace of Pentacles: entities only if the product needs them
cards.prompt:
Define product data. Analysis only — no code.

Output: entities and fields; validation; where stored (file, local, DB, cloud); external contracts — only if needed.

Do not force a DB, REST, or ORM on a desktop/local app without need. If storage is unnecessary — say so. Do not invent entities outside scope.
Next: “What we build with”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — data defined or storage not needed
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: What we build with
cards.description: Chariot: simplest structure and stack after reading the repo
cards.prompt:
First read the repository and current dependencies. Propose the simplest structure and stack for the job.

Output: folders and key files; language and libraries; what to reuse from open source instead of writing from scratch; risks and a rollback idea.

Boring working beats trendy architecture. Do not add microservices or containers for a simple project. Do not invent missing dependencies. Do not break what already works.
Next: “Code rules”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — structure and stack proposed
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: Code rules
cards.prompt:
Check existing rule files: AGENTS.md (project rules) and .cursor/rules/*.mdc. Propose minimal consistent edits, or a base set if none exist.

Do not create a legacy .cursorrules by default. Do not duplicate existing rules. Change files only when asked. 5–10 simple rules are enough: style, naming, what is forbidden.
Next: “Plan review”.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, or files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; flattery; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — rules checked or proposed
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: Plan review
cards.prompt:
Score the specification honestly — no flattery.

Check: clear goal; completeness (brief, scope, UI, data, architecture, rules); excess; obvious security holes; whether acceptance criteria are testable.

Project quality score 0–10: 0–6 fix before code; 7–8 can start; 9–10 excellent. Do not inflate. For 9–10 give 3 facts why the spec is strong. Below 7 — name one specification card as next.

Reply: score N/10 · verdict · pros · cons · top-3 fixes.
Score ≥7 — “Ready to code?”. Below 7 — fix the named card.

The project may be empty — judge only what exists.
Forbidden: inventing facts or holes; inflating score out of pity; giving 9–10 without three facts; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

Always end with this line (N = your 0-10 score):
KEYCODE_SCORE: N
If you cannot score due to missing data, add a second line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA

cards.title: Ready to code?
cards.description: Judgement: gate into Hobby or Production
cards.prompt:
Check readiness to code. Do not PASS if anything is missing. Do not invent artifacts.

Required: goal and users; scope and happy path; UI with states; data where needed; architecture; rules or a base set; acceptance criteria; plan-review score ≥7.

Do not guess the mode. Ask explicitly if not chosen:
- Hobby — fast simple project;
- Production — stricter, with review and merge readiness.

The project may be empty — no fact = not PASS.
Forbidden: inventing evidence; PASSing out of pity or because “the idea is good”; flattery.

End with exactly two lines.
Hobby:
KEYCODE_GATE: PASS
KEYCODE_NEXT: lazy-v1/plan

Production:
KEYCODE_GATE: PASS
KEYCODE_NEXT: pro-v1/plan

Not ready (replace brief with the missing card id: scope, ux, data-contracts, architecture, project-rules, risk-review):
KEYCODE_GATE: FAIL
KEYCODE_NEXT: spec-v1/brief

cards.title: Recap
cards.description: High Priestess: goal, decided, open, next
cards.prompt:
Read this chat. Do not write or change code.

Four short blocks (1–3 bullets each):
1. Goal
2. Decided — which artifacts are ready
3. Open — what is still missing
4. Next step — one card: Why and for whom / What we do / How it looks / What we store / What we build with / Code rules / Plan review / Ready to code? — or move to Work

If the specification is not ready — say so.
Do not add KEYCODE_SCORE, KEYCODE_GATE, KEYCODE_NEXT, or KEYCODE_STATUS lines.

The project may be empty — write only what is visible in chat.
Forbidden: inventing completed work; writing or changing code; adding KEYCODE_SCORE, KEYCODE_GATE, KEYCODE_NEXT, or KEYCODE_STATUS lines.
